Hi Lucas / Maya,

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. Per our notes, I put together a short model shortlist and an initial sizing sketch to help the implementation team plan capacity for your SearchAssist product (embedding + generative clarification flow). Attaching the token profile and the sizing CSV for reference.

High-level assumptions (from your intake):
- Active users (DAU): 18k; peak concurrent users: ~210
- Average prompt length (search + metadata): 220 tokens
- Typical model response: 120 tokens (clarifications) / 350 tokens (multi-step answer)
- Approx split: 65% embeddings calls (short), 35% chat/generation calls (longer context)

Model shortlist (recommended variants for pilot):
1) redwood-13b-8k (quantized) — balanced quality vs cost; good for multi-step summaries and few-shot prompts
2) meta/llama-2-70b-chat-8k (server variant) — higher quality for complex summarization; more expensive, consider for canary of heavy users
3) mistral-instruct-7b-32k (reduced precision) — strong cost-to-quality for longer context flows if you expect >8k history

Context-length guidance:
- Baseline: 4k context sufficient for ~85% of clarification flows
- Long-history sessions: provision 16k for user sessions that include conversation + 3 prior documents (expected ~10% of traffic)

Initial token-volume estimates (monthly):
- Embeddings: 18k DAU * 0.65 * 40 tokens * 30 days ≈ 14M tokens/month
- Generation: 18k DAU * 0.35 * 300 tokens * 30 days ≈ 56.7M tokens/month
- Total (pilot): ~71M tokens/month (estimate)

Ask: can you confirm DAU/peak-concurrency numbers and whether you expect heavier multi-doc sessions beyond the 10% noted? That will shift whether we recommend 16k vs 32k context on day 1.

Next steps I propose:
- You: confirm DAU & heavy-session % by Monday (18 Jan)
- We (solutions + infra): respond with a dedicated capacity recommendation (GPU type, pool size, expected latency SLOs) and a cost ballpark
- Schedule: technical kickoff with your infra team the week of 25 Jan

Subject: Internal: Northridge sizing recommendation (draft)

Team — looping you in to draft the capacity recommendation. Key inputs from Lucas: DAU up to 25k, peak concurrent ~300 during spikes, heavy sessions ~18%, latency SLOs as below.

Recap of ask: which model(s) to pilot and what Dedicated/hosted footprint to reserve to hit the SLOs and cost targets for MVP.

My read (draft):
- Pilot model: redwood-13b-8k (quantized) as primary. Rationale: best compromise on token cost vs quality and it hits sub-600ms 95th for short replies on 2x A100-80GB when requests are batched at 8–12 tokens/step.
- Canary model for high-quality lane: llama-2-70b-chat-8k in a separate pool (1x A100-80GB per 4 concurrent long-form streams) — enable automatic fallback to redwood-13b during capacity pressure.
- Long-context candidate: mistral-instruct-7b-32k on an 80GB-quantized profile for sessions requiring >8k context; expect 10–15% higher latency vs 8k runs.

Sizing estimate (pilot, 25k DAU peak):
- Embeddings traffic: provision a small autoscaling pool of 2x T4-equivalent instances (stateless) — cheap and scales horizontally
- Generation traffic (redwood-13b primary): 3x A100-80GB reserved (handles sustained 240 concurrent short-gen streams with batching), burst pool of 1 extra node for spikes
- Canary pool (llama-70b): 1x A100-80GB reserved, scale to 2 for bursts (expected lower utilization initially)

Cost / throughput notes (rough):
- Expected monthly token throughput ~85–95M tokens/month if spikes hit 25k DAU; margin included
- Estimated GPU hours: 3x A100 reserved (720 hours/mo each) + canary + embedding autoscale. We'll produce a ballpark cost after Connor pulls instance pricing and our reserved discount tiers.

Operational recommendations:
- Start with separate pools for 8k vs 32k contexts to simplify memory tuning and kernel selection. 
- Enable prefix KV caching for repeated doc contexts to drop token processing on heavy users.
- Set a fallback policy: if the canary (70b) exceeds 80% CPU/GPU alloc, route to 13b with a quality warning header in response.

Connor / Rishi — can you validate the 3x A100 assumption and the expected 95th latency with our current kernel sets? If so I’ll fold this into a message back to Northridge with next steps and a proposed tech kickoff window.

—Jasmine

Hi Lucas / Maya — thanks for the quick replies and context. Based on your updated traffic expectations (up to 25k DAU, heavy sessions ~18%) we recommend the following plan for the pilot: 

Plan (pilot, 6–8 week):
1) Models & pools
   - Primary: redwood-13b-8k (quantized) on a reserved pool of 3x A100-80GB
   - Canary/high-quality lane: llama-2-70b-chat-8k in a separate pool with 1 reserved A100, autoscale to 2 for bursts
   - Long-context: mistral-instruct-7b-32k enabled in a different pool; enable only for tagged power-user sessions to constrain cost
2) Context strategy
   - Default context: 4k for general users
   - Heavy sessions: 16k enabled via tag; we'll route to the 32k pool only if cost/quality tradeoff justifies the additional memory during the pilot
3) Capacity & SLOs
   - Target: <600ms 95th for short replies (with batching); <1400ms 95th for long-form
   - Fallback: automatic degrade from 70b -> 13b with response header explaining fallback and telemetry turned on
4) Next steps / schedule
   - We’ll turn the pools on in Dedicated test environment: Wed 27 Jan
   - Technical kickoff with your infra + SREs: Thu 28 Jan (30–45 min)
   - Deliverables before kickoff: Connor will share cost scenarios and an autoscale policy; Monica will share updated token-profile with the 18% heavy-session weighting reflected
If that plan looks good I’ll send a calendar invite for the 28th kick-off and include the materials.

Thanks — looking forward to working with you.
